records.context: Two wiring details are load-bearing; both are the same contract :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents, and this function used to get them wrong:

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two wiring details are load-bearing; both are the same contract :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents, and this function used to get them wrong:
records.translation: Dos detalles de conexión son esenciales; ambos forman parte del mismo contrato que documenta :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread`, y esta función antes los hacía mal:

records.context: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` uses a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created on the GUI thread. That gives it GUI thread affinity. A queued ``quit()`` goes to the *GUI* event queue rather than the worker queue. The GUI thread immediately enters ``thread.wait()`` during the "drain before closing" behavior in ``ConsolePanel.shutdown``. This blocks the event that would stop the worker and waits for the full timeout even though the worker has finished. ``QThread::quit`` is thread-safe, so the worker thread may call it directly.
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` is a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created here, on the GUI thread, so it is GUI-affine — a queued ``quit()`` is posted to the *GUI* thread's event queue, not to the worker's. Measured: with a queued connection, a GUI thread that goes straight into ``thread.wait()`` (which is exactly what ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` and every "drain before closing" path does) waits out its whole timeout on a worker that has already finished, because the event that would stop the thread is sitting behind the wait. ``QThread::quit`` is explicitly thread-safe, so calling it inline from the worker thread is correct.
records.translation: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` es una **DirectConnection**. El objeto QThread se crea aquí, en el hilo de la GUI, por lo que tiene afinidad con la GUI: un ``quit()`` en cola se publica en la cola de eventos del hilo de la *GUI*, no en la del hilo de trabajo. Medición: con una conexión en cola, un hilo de la GUI que pasa directamente a ``thread.wait()`` (que es exactamente lo que hacen ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` y toda ruta "drain before closing" (vaciar antes de cerrar)) agota todo su tiempo de espera con un hilo de trabajo que ya ha terminado, porque el evento que detendría el hilo está esperando detrás de la espera. ``QThread::quit`` es explícitamente seguro entre hilos, por lo que llamarlo directamente desde el hilo de trabajo es correcto.

records.context: There is deliberately **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. The worker's affinity is the background execution unit, so a deferred delete is posted into a loop that is stopping, while the panel drops the object's last Python reference from the main GUI execution path — two owners, one object. ``bridge.make_thread``'s ownership essay records the gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) and the measurement: 3 crashes in 8 executions. A PySide6 object built in Python is already owned by Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` hold it in ``_retired`` until the independent execution path has exited and free it there, on the independent execution path that holds it.
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: There is deliberately **no** ``worker.deleteLater``. The worker's affinity is the worker thread, so a deferred delete is posted into a loop that is stopping, while the panel drops the object's last Python reference from the GUI thread — two owners, one object. ``bridge.make_thread``'s ownership essay records the gdb trace (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) and the measurement: 3 crashes in 8 runs. A PySide6 object built in Python is already owned by Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` hold it in ``_retired`` until the thread has exited and free it there, on the thread that holds it.
records.translation: Deliberadamente **no** hay ``worker.deleteLater``. La afinidad del hilo de trabajo es el propio hilo de trabajo, así que un borrado diferido se publica en un bucle que se está deteniendo, mientras el panel suelta la última referencia de Python al objeto desde el hilo de la GUI: dos propietarios para un solo objeto. El texto sobre propiedad de ``bridge.make_thread`` registra la traza de gdb (``QThread -> sendPostedEvents -> ~QObject -> Sbk_GetPyOverride``) y la medición: 3 fallos en 8 ejecuciones. Un objeto de PySide6 creado en Python ya es propiedad de Python; ``ConsolePanel``/``AIChatPanel`` lo mantienen en ``_retired`` hasta que el hilo ha terminado y lo liberan allí, en el hilo que lo contiene.

A wallpaper is not a figure, and a stray scale bar reads as an artefact, so its ``source_crop`` cuts above it. records.context: These are not a procedural sky of point stars — ``cell.png``'s cyan core fills most of the frame and measures 0.236 in the brightest text-line-sized window, which is far too bright to put white-on-nothing text over. So each master is dimmed at build time by a factor solved from the palette: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returns the brightest a bare window background may be before some role that gets painted straight onto it (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, the status hues) drops below its WCAG minimum, and :func:`solve_dim` scales the image in linear light until the brightest :data:`TEXT_WINDOW`-sized region lands on that number less :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.

records.source: These are not a procedural sky of point stars — ``cell.png``'s cyan core fills most of the frame and measures 0.236 in the brightest text-line-sized window, which is far too bright to put white-on-nothing text over. So each master is dimmed at build time by a factor solved from the palette: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returns the brightest a bare window background may be before some role that gets painted straight onto it (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, the status hues) drops below its WCAG minimum, and :func:`solve_dim` scales the image in linear light until the brightest :data:`TEXT_WINDOW`-sized region lands on that number less :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.
records.translation: No se trata de un cielo procedimental de estrellas puntuales: el núcleo cian de ``cell.png`` ocupa la mayor parte del fotograma y mide 0.236 en la ventana del tamaño de una línea de texto más brillante, lo que es demasiado brillante para colocar encima texto blanco sin fondo. Por eso, cada imagen maestra se atenúa durante la construcción con un factor calculado a partir de la paleta: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` devuelve el brillo máximo que puede tener el fondo desnudo de una ventana antes de que algún rol pintado directamente sobre él (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, los tonos de estado) caiga por debajo de su mínimo WCAG, y :func:`solve_dim` escala la imagen en luz lineal hasta que la región más brillante del tamaño de :data:`TEXT_WINDOW` alcanza ese valor menos :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.

records.translation: Reutiliza el directorio de caché de ``space``, sus límites de tamaño y su contrato "never raise, fall back to something" (nunca lanzar una excepción, recurrir siempre a una alternativa), de modo que, desde fuera, un fondo fotográfico y uno generado se comportan exactamente igual. Lo nuevo es lo que necesitan las fotografías y no los píxeles procedimentales: un presupuesto de decodificación, una política de recorte y una comprobación medida de la legibilidad.

records.context: The split keeps the model testable. Five later features build on the layer model — ROI shapes read by Measure, a counting points layer, a label brush with timelapse track curation, orthogonal views with dimension sliders, and a synchronised comparison grid — and every one of them is a change to the model with a small widget on top. Putting the compositing rules in a ``paintEvent`` would make all five untestable without a running ``QApplication``.

records.source: The split keeps the model testable. Five later features build on the layer model — ROI shapes read by Measure, a counting points layer, a label brush with timelapse track curation, orthogonal views with dimension sliders, and a synchronised comparison grid — and every one of them is a change to the model with a small widget on top. Putting the compositing rules in a ``paintEvent`` would make all five untestable without a running ``QApplication``.
records.translation: Esta separación mantiene el modelo comprobable. Cinco funciones posteriores se basan en el modelo de capas (formas de ROI que lee Measure, una capa de puntos para recuento, un pincel de etiquetas con curación de trayectorias en series temporales, vistas ortogonales con controles deslizantes de dimensión y una cuadrícula de comparación sincronizada), y cada una de ellas es un cambio en el modelo con un pequeño widget encima. Poner las reglas de composición en un ``paintEvent`` haría que las cinco no pudieran probarse sin una ``QApplication`` en ejecución.

records.context: :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview._ZoomView` is the right answer when the thing being shown is a finished pixmap: it scales what it was given. Here the zoom is a property of the world, not of the picture — zooming in means :meth:`spacr.layers.Canvas.zoomed` and a fresh render at the new resolution, which is how the labels layer stays crisp at 8× and how the orthogonal-view item gets its slice sliders for free. So the canvas owns a :class:`~spacr.layers.Canvas` and paints; the array→pixmap step still goes through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.numpy_to_qpixmap`, and file loading through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_preview_image`, rather than growing a third copy of either.

So the canvas owns a :class:`~spacr.layers.Canvas` and paints; the array→pixmap step still goes through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.numpy_to_qpixmap`, and file loading through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_preview_image`, rather than growing a third copy of either.
records.translation: :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview._ZoomView` es la solución adecuada cuando lo que se muestra es un pixmap terminado: escala lo que recibe. Aquí el zoom es una propiedad del mundo, no de la imagen: acercar significa :meth:`spacr.layers.Canvas.zoomed` y un nuevo renderizado a la nueva resolución, que es como la capa de etiquetas se mantiene nítida a 8× y como el elemento de vista ortogonal obtiene sin coste sus controles deslizantes de corte. records.context: ``clear VRAM`` ``torch.cuda.empty_cache()``, which hands the CUDA driver back the blocks torch reserved and is no longer using, plus releasing any model reference spaCR itself is holding (:data:`MODEL_RELEASERS`). **It cannot reclaim another process's VRAM** — no process can — and it cannot free a tensor an executing spaCR job is still using, which is the point rather than a limitation.

records.source: ``clear VRAM`` ``torch.cuda.empty_cache()``, which hands the CUDA driver back the blocks torch reserved and is no longer using, plus releasing any model reference spaCR itself is holding (:data:`MODEL_RELEASERS`). **It cannot reclaim another process's VRAM** — no process can — and it cannot free a tensor a running spaCR job is still using, which is the point rather than a limitation.
records.translation: ``clear VRAM`` ``torch.cuda.empty_cache()``, que devuelve al controlador CUDA los bloques que torch reservó y ya no usa, además de liberar cualquier referencia a modelos que mantenga el propio spaCR (:data:`MODEL_RELEASERS`). **No puede recuperar la VRAM de otro proceso** (ningún proceso puede), y no puede liberar un tensor que un trabajo de spaCR en ejecución sigue usando, lo cual es precisamente el objetivo y no una limitación.

records.context: ``clear CPU`` Releases parked background execution units that have since exited (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), lets Qt's global pool retire its idle independent execution paths, and lowers spaCR's own library worker-count limits (torch, OpenCV) to a floor. It retires *idle* capacity only: work that is queued or executing is left exactly where it is.

records.source: ``clear CPU`` Releases parked worker threads that have since exited (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), lets Qt's global pool retire its idle threads, and lowers spaCR's own library thread counts (torch, OpenCV) to a floor. It retires *idle* capacity only: work that is queued or running is left exactly where it is.
records.translation: ``clear CPU`` Libera los hilos de trabajo aparcados que ya han terminado (:func:`spacr.qt.bridge.prune_parked_threads`), permite que el grupo global de Qt retire sus hilos inactivos y reduce hasta un mínimo el número de hilos de las bibliotecas del propio spaCR (torch, OpenCV). Solo retira capacidad *inactiva*: el trabajo en cola o en ejecución se deja exactamente donde está.

records.context: **No process is ever killed.** Not by name, not by "python processes using a lot of memory", not spaCR's own children. There is no ``os.kill``, no ``signal``, no ``subprocess``, no ``Process.terminate()``, no ``QThread.terminate()`` anywhere in this module or reachable from it. The Qt layer removed ``QThread.terminate()`` outright; a stubborn independent execution path is *parked* by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, and that is the strongest thing any of this may do.

There is no ``os.kill``, no ``signal``, no ``subprocess``, no ``Process.terminate()``, no ``QThread.terminate()`` anywhere in this module or reachable from it. The Qt layer removed ``QThread.terminate()`` outright; a stubborn thread is *parked* by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, and that is the strongest thing any of this may do.
records.translation: **Nunca se mata ningún proceso.** Ni por nombre, ni por "python processes using a lot of memory", ni los propios hijos de spaCR. No hay ``os.kill``, ni ``signal``, ni ``subprocess``, ni ``Process.terminate()``, ni ``QThread.terminate()`` en ninguna parte de este módulo ni en nada accesible desde él. La capa de Qt eliminó ``QThread.terminate()`` por completo; un hilo que se resiste queda *aparcado* por :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, y eso es lo más contundente que puede hacer cualquier parte de esto.

records.context: :data:`TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE` exposes the frame so that *empty sky* — not the mean — lands on :data:`TARGET_SKY_LUMA`, deliberately, so that a sun stays blown out instead of dragging the whole frame to black. records.translation: :data:`TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE` expone el fotograma de modo que el *cielo vacío* (no la media) quede en :data:`TARGET_SKY_LUMA`, deliberadamente, para que un sol siga sobreexpuesto en lugar de arrastrar todo el fotograma hacia el negro. Entendido como una afirmación sobre una única exposición global, esto es ahora totalmente incompatible con el límite, y las dos formas obvias de forzarlo dan imágenes arruinadas. Volver a calcular la exposición, o atenuar el fotograma terminado con :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.solve_dim`, requiere un factor de 0.064-0.108; ambas llevan el propio percentil 40 del cielo de 0.00091 a 0.00000, es decir, todas las estrellas débiles y toda la nebulosa pasan a negro puro, y el píxel máximo cae de 236-252 a 67-90. Medido, renderizado y observado: una mancha gris oscura.

records.context: The reconciliation is that the two rules are about different things. The exposure anchor is about a *pixel with nothing in it*; the WCAG limit is about the mean over a **region the size of a line of text** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), which is the point :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` already makes about photographs — every photograph has a white pixel somewhere and it is a bright *patch* that makes a caption unreadable. A 3 px star inside a 202x48 px text window moves that window's mean by a quarter of one per cent; the whole starfield measured on its own comes to 0.0007-0.0067, i.e. 1-11 % of the limit. A 207 px sun disc fills the window completely and cannot.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The reconciliation is that the two rules are about different things. The exposure anchor is about a *pixel with nothing in it*; the WCAG limit is about the mean over a **region the size of a line of text** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), which is the point :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` already makes about photographs — every photograph has a white pixel somewhere and it is a bright *patch* that makes a caption unreadable. A 3 px star inside a 202x48 px text window moves that window's mean by a quarter of one per cent; the whole starfield measured on its own comes to 0.0007-0.0067, i.e. 1-11 % of the limit. A 207 px sun disc fills the window completely and cannot.
records.translation: La conciliación consiste en que las dos reglas tratan de cosas distintas. El anclaje de exposición se refiere a un *píxel sin nada dentro*; el límite WCAG se refiere a la media sobre una **región del tamaño de una línea de texto** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), que es lo que :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` ya señala sobre las fotografías: toda fotografía tiene algún píxel blanco, y lo que hace ilegible un pie de texto es una *zona* brillante. Una estrella de 3 px dentro de una ventana de texto de 202x48 px desplaza la media de esa ventana en una cuarta parte de un uno por ciento; el campo de estrellas completo, medido por sí solo, da 0.0007-0.0067, es decir, 1-11 % del límite. Un disco solar de 207 px llena la ventana por completo y no puede cumplirlo.

records.context: So the exposure anchor is kept exactly as it was — the sky background is unchanged, to the byte — and the limit is enforced where it is actually violated, by compressing the highlights of the **smooth** layers only (:func:`_compress_highlights`, applied to nebula + galaxy + sun + bloom, never to the starfield). The sun therefore does get noticeably darker, which is the accepted cost; the galaxy is barely touched because it was never the offender; the stars keep white cores and diffraction spikes. :func:`_enforce_legibility` then measures the finished frame with the same :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` used on the photographs and applies whatever residual dim is left, so the guarantee is a measurement and not an argument.
records.label: spacr.qt.space#17
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So the exposure anchor is kept exactly as it was — the sky background is unchanged, to the byte — and the limit is enforced where it is actually violated, by compressing the highlights of the **smooth** layers only (:func:`_compress_highlights`, applied to nebula + galaxy + sun + bloom, never to the starfield). The sun therefore does get noticeably darker, which is the accepted cost; the galaxy is barely touched because it was never the offender; the stars keep white cores and diffraction spikes. :func:`_enforce_legibility` then measures the finished frame with the same :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` used on the photographs and applies whatever residual dim is left, so the guarantee is a measurement and not an argument.
records.translation: Por eso el anclaje de exposición se mantiene exactamente igual (el fondo del cielo no cambia, ni en un byte) y el límite se impone donde realmente se incumple, comprimiendo las altas luces solo de las capas **suaves** (:func:`_compress_highlights`, aplicada a nebulosa + galaxia + sol + resplandor, nunca al campo de estrellas). Por tanto, el sol sí se oscurece de forma apreciable, que es el coste aceptado; la galaxia apenas se modifica porque nunca fue la culpable; las estrellas conservan sus núcleos blancos y sus picos de difracción. A continuación, :func:`_enforce_legibility` mide el fotograma terminado con la misma :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` que se usa en las fotografías y aplica la atenuación residual que quede, de modo que la garantía es una medición y no un argumento.

records.source: :func:`exposure_target` is a *linear-light* relative luminance of the finished image. ``_tone_map``'s output is written straight to 8-bit without a gamma encode, so it is an **sRGB signal value**, and the two are a transfer function apart — the 0.0586 limit is a mid-dark grey around ``#444444``, not a 6 % signal. Encode first, then invert ``1 - exp(-x·E)``.
records.translation: :func:`exposure_target` es una luminancia relativa en *luz lineal* de la imagen terminada. La salida de ``_tone_map`` se escribe directamente a 8 bits sin codificación gamma, por lo que es un **valor de señal sRGB**, y entre ambos media una función de transferencia: el límite 0.0586 es un gris medio-oscuro en torno a ``#444444``, no una señal del 6 %. Primero se codifica y después se invierte ``1 - exp(-x·E)``.

records.source: ``inf`` when there is nothing to solve for — a palette that admits no wallpaper at all (:func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` is *negative* for the light theme) or a zero exposure. Callers read that as "no ceiling", never as "clamp everything to zero". A palette that admits a white wallpaper lands on a ceiling far above anything the generators emit, which comes to the same thing without a second branch to leave untested.
records.translation: ``inf`` cuando no hay nada que calcular: una paleta que no admite ningún fondo de pantalla (:func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` es *negativa* para el tema claro) o una exposición cero. Quienes llaman lo interpretan como "no ceiling" (sin límite), nunca como "clamp everything to zero" (limitar todo a cero). Una paleta que admite un fondo de pantalla blanco da un límite muy por encima de cualquier valor que emitan los generadores, lo que equivale a lo mismo sin una segunda rama que quede sin probar.

records.source: An interactive tooltip has three requirements, handled here as follows:
records.translation: Una información emergente interactiva tiene tres requisitos, que aquí se resuelven así:

records.context: It must not disappear while the pointer moves toward it. The pointer has to cross the gap between the row and the panel, and a plain leave-event dismissal closes it mid-journey, which makes the Install link unreachable. The hide is a timer, the timer is cancelled on entry, and while it is pending the cursor is checked against the corridor -- the union of the anchor's rectangle and the panel's -- so travelling through the gap re-arms the timer instead of firing it. See :meth:`AvailabilityPanel. _maybe_hide`.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.availability_panel#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: It must not disappear while the pointer moves toward it. The pointer has to cross the gap between the row and the panel, and a plain leave-event dismissal closes it mid-journey, which makes the Install link unreachable. The hide is a timer, the timer is cancelled on entry, and while it is pending the cursor is checked against the corridor -- the union of the anchor's rectangle and the panel's -- so travelling through the gap re-arms the timer instead of firing it. See :meth:`AvailabilityPanel. _maybe_hide`.
records.translation: No debe desaparecer mientras el puntero se desplaza hacia ella. El puntero tiene que cruzar el hueco entre la fila y el panel, y un cierre simple con el evento de salida lo cierra a mitad de camino, lo que hace inalcanzable el enlace Install. La ocultación es un temporizador, el temporizador se cancela al entrar y, mientras está pendiente, se comprueba si el cursor está dentro del corredor (la unión del rectángulo del ancla y el del panel), de modo que atravesar el hueco rearma el temporizador en lugar de dispararlo. Consulte :meth:`AvailabilityPanel. _maybe_hide`.

records.source: The container is made transparent rather than coloured. The application sheet carries a blanket ``QWidget { background-color: bg }``, so any untagged container paints an opaque rectangle -- and a plain widget holding a rounded panel is exactly that, a square of window colour behind rounded corners. Colouring it only changes which colour the rectangle is.
records.translation: El contenedor se hace transparente en lugar de colorearlo. La hoja de estilos de la aplicación incluye un ``QWidget { background-color: bg }`` general, por lo que cualquier contenedor sin etiquetar pinta un rectángulo opaco, y un widget simple que contiene un panel redondeado es exactamente eso: un cuadrado del color de la ventana detrás de las esquinas redondeadas. Colorearlo solo cambia el color del rectángulo.

records.context: Rank per-object measurements by class-separation performance.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Rank per-object measurements by class-separation performance.
records.translation: Clasifica las mediciones por objeto según su capacidad de separar clases.

records.context: The default statistic is the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), computed from the Mann–Whitney U statistic. Results are reported as the unit-free separation ``|2·AUC − 1|`` in ``[0, 1]`` together with the direction of the class difference. AUC is rank based and therefore invariant under monotonic transformations; it does not require normality, equal variance or symmetry. These properties allow measurements with different units and distributions to be compared in one ranking.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The default statistic is the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), computed from the Mann–Whitney U statistic. Results are reported as the unit-free separation ``|2·AUC − 1|`` in ``[0, 1]`` together with the direction of the class difference. AUC is rank based and therefore invariant under monotonic transformations; it does not require normality, equal variance or symmetry. These properties allow measurements with different units and distributions to be compared in one ranking.
records.translation: El estadístico predeterminado es el área bajo la curva característica operativa del receptor (AUC), calculada a partir del estadístico U de Mann–Whitney. Los resultados se expresan como la separación adimensional ``|2·AUC − 1|`` en ``[0, 1]`` junto con el sentido de la diferencia entre clases. El AUC se basa en rangos y, por tanto, es invariante frente a transformaciones monótonas; no requiere normalidad, igualdad de varianzas ni simetría. Estas propiedades permiten comparar en una sola clasificación mediciones con unidades y distribuciones diferentes.

records.context: AUC represents the probability that a randomly selected object from one class has a higher value than a randomly selected object from the other class. It detects stochastic ordering but can miss distribution-shape differences. For example, classes with the same centre but different spread can have an AUC of 0.5 despite differing distributions. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) statistic is therefore computed for every feature. A high KS statistic combined with AUC near 0.5 sets :attr:`FeatureScore.is_shape_not_shift`.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: AUC represents the probability that a randomly selected object from one class has a higher value than a randomly selected object from the other class. It detects stochastic ordering but can miss distribution-shape differences. For example, classes with the same centre but different spread can have an AUC of 0.5 despite differing distributions. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) statistic is therefore computed for every feature. A high KS statistic combined with AUC near 0.5 sets :attr:`FeatureScore.is_shape_not_shift`.
records.translation: El AUC representa la probabilidad de que un objeto seleccionado al azar de una clase tenga un valor mayor que un objeto seleccionado al azar de la otra clase. Detecta el orden estocástico, pero puede pasar por alto diferencias en la forma de la distribución. Por ejemplo, clases con el mismo centro pero distinta dispersión pueden tener un AUC de 0.5 aunque sus distribuciones difieran. Por ello, se calcula el estadístico de Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) para cada característica. Un estadístico KS alto combinado con un AUC cercano a 0.5 activa :attr:`FeatureScore.is_shape_not_shift`.

records.translation: :attr:`ExplorerSpec.n_permutations` activa una calibración por permutación a nivel de familia. records.source: Returns True once the PNG — the raster the GUI actually displays — is on disk. A failed *sibling PDF* does not turn that into False, and the asymmetry is deliberate rather than sloppy: the callers turn False into "no pixmap, no thumbnail", so reporting a missing export that way would delete the figure from the gallery over a file nothing has asked for yet. It is logged at WARNING instead, and :meth:`FigureQueue._request_pdf_refinement` notices the absent page, says so, and stops waiting for a render that will never arrive.
records.translation: Devuelve True en cuanto el PNG (el ráster que la GUI muestra realmente) está en disco. Un fallo del *PDF asociado* no lo convierte en False, y la asimetría es deliberada y no un descuido: quienes llaman interpretan False como "no pixmap, no thumbnail" (sin pixmap ni miniatura), de modo que comunicar así una exportación ausente eliminaría la figura de la galería por un archivo que nadie ha pedido todavía. En su lugar se registra con nivel WARNING, y :meth:`FigureQueue._request_pdf_refinement` detecta la página ausente, lo indica y deja de esperar un renderizado que nunca llegará.

records.translation: Se toma una instantánea serializada de la figura para que Cancel tenga algo a lo que volver: aplicar en directo sin salida es una trampa; el usuario arrastra un selector numérico para ver qué hace y ya no existe un "as it was" (como estaba). El tamaño de texto propio de la figura se guarda por separado, porque Cancel restaura la figura copiando los ejes desde la instantánea en lugar de intercambiar el objeto, de modo que, de lo contrario, ese atributo sobreviviría a la anulación de todo aquello a lo que se aplica.

records.translation: La pestaña Estadística solo aparece para una figura que compara grupos: ofrecer una prueba t sobre un gráfico Q-Q sería invitar a comunicar una cifra que no significa nada. La pestaña UMAP solo aparece para una figura que lleva la proyección a partir de la cual se dibujó; sin ella, "live" (en directo) significaría volver a ejecutar la reducción y todos los puntos se moverían.

records.source: This fallback supports figures without a ``_spacr_replot`` payload by reading plotted values from bars, scatter collections, and data lines on a single axes. Figures created by :func:`spacr.plot.create_grouped_plot` use their attached source frame instead of this fallback.
records.translation: Esta alternativa admite figuras sin carga ``_spacr_replot`` leyendo los valores representados de barras, colecciones de dispersión y líneas de datos en unos únicos ejes. The node count and nesting depth are capped as well (:data:`MAX_NODES`, :data:`MAX_DEPTH`), so a pathological expression is refused at parse time rather than during a redraw.

records.source: Numbers are read as **floats**, always: ``9 ** 9 ** 9`` with Python integers is a multi-second allocation of a number with 300 million digits — a denial of service typed in eleven characters — and with floats it is ``inf`` in a nanosecond. The node count and nesting depth are capped as well (:data:`MAX_NODES`, :data:`MAX_DEPTH`), so a pathological expression is refused at parse time rather than during a redraw.
records.translation: Los números se leen siempre como **flotantes**: ``9 ** 9 ** 9`` con enteros de Python supone varios segundos de asignación de un número de 300 millones de dígitos (una denegación de servicio escrita en once caracteres), y con flotantes es ``inf`` en un nanosegundo. El número de nodos y la profundidad de anidamiento también están limitados (:data:`MAX_NODES`, :data:`MAX_DEPTH`), de modo que una expresión patológica se rechaza durante el análisis en lugar de durante un redibujado.

records.context: **The whole table, never the filtered view.** ``zscore(area)`` computed over whatever the Local Data Filter currently shows would change every time a slider moved, so the column would not be stable: two charts drawn a second apart would disagree, and an exported CSV would record one arbitrary moment. records.context: Two rules apply to what the preview reports.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two rules apply to what the preview reports.
records.translation: Se aplican dos reglas a lo que informa la vista previa.

records.context: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. So that a velocity is never read in the wrong unit, the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of silently using the 1.78 px/µm default.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Units.** The assay converts pixels per frame into physical units with ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` and only when *both* are known; otherwise it reports ``px/frame``. So that a velocity is never read in the wrong unit, the calibration fields start **unset**, every velocity carries its unit, and while the calibration is unknown the panel says so in words instead of silently using the 1.78 px/µm default.
records.translation: **Unidades.** El ensayo convierte píxeles por fotograma en unidades físicas con ``factor = (1 / pixels_per_um) * (60 / seconds_per_frame)`` y solo cuando se conocen *ambos*; de lo contrario, informa en ``px/frame``. Para que nunca se lea una velocidad en la unidad equivocada, los campos de calibración empiezan **sin establecer**, cada velocidad lleva su unidad y, mientras la calibración es desconocida, el panel lo indica con palabras en lugar de usar en silencio el valor predeterminado de 1.78 px/µm.

records.context: The expensive half (reading merged arrays and extracting centroids) runs once in a background execution unit and is **cached** as a point table. Every metric setting — minimum length, max displacement, straightness threshold, and both calibration fields — recomputes from that cached table on the main GUI execution path, instantly.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.motility_preview#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The expensive half (reading merged arrays and extracting centroids) runs once in a worker thread and is **cached** as a point table. Every metric setting — minimum length, max displacement, straightness threshold, and both calibration fields — recomputes from that cached table on the GUI thread, instantly.
records.translation: La mitad costosa (leer los arrays combinados y extraer los centroides) se ejecuta una vez en un hilo de trabajo y se **almacena en caché** como tabla de puntos. Cada ajuste de métrica (longitud mínima, desplazamiento máximo, umbral de rectitud y ambos campos de calibración) se recalcula de forma instantánea a partir de esa tabla en caché en el hilo de la GUI.

records.source: A single frame whose steps in and out both exceed ``max_displacement`` while its neighbours are within it is a segmentation glitch, and the assay interpolates it. Any *remaining* step over the limit means the track links two different objects, and the assay drops the whole track. This reproduces both, so the preview's track count matches a run's.
records.translation: Un único fotograma cuyos pasos de entrada y salida superan ambos ``max_displacement`` mientras que sus vecinos están dentro del límite es un fallo de segmentación, y el ensayo lo interpola. Cualquier paso *restante* por encima del límite significa que la trayectoria une dos objetos distintos, y el ensayo descarta toda la trayectoria. Esto reproduce ambos casos, de modo que el número de trayectorias de la vista previa coincide con el de una ejecución.

records.source: Why the scores plot is a GraphCanvas

records.context: A PCA scores plot is a scatter of two continuous columns that a user wants to colour by ``gene``, facet by ``plateID``, and brush to pull a cluster into Annotate. That is the Graph Builder, exactly, with the two columns computed rather than measured. So :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` appends ``PC1…PCk`` to the source frame and :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` is a :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` subclass that draws arrows on top.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_view#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A PCA scores plot is a scatter of two continuous columns that a user wants to colour by ``gene``, facet by ``plateID``, and brush to pull a cluster into Annotate. That is the Graph Builder, exactly, with the two columns computed rather than measured. So :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` appends ``PC1…PCk`` to the source frame and :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` is a :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` subclass that draws arrows on top.
records.translation: Un gráfico de puntuaciones de PCA es un diagrama de dispersión de dos columnas continuas que el usuario quiere colorear por ``gene``, dividir en facetas por ``plateID`` y seleccionar con el pincel para llevar un grupo a Annotate. Eso es exactamente el Graph Builder, con las dos columnas calculadas en lugar de medidas. Por eso :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` añade ``PC1…PCk`` a la tabla de origen y :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` es una subclase de :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` que dibuja flechas encima.

records.context: Rows and columns are the **cartesian product** of their structured-data names' levels, empty combinations included, exactly as :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` draws empty panels: a table read by position needs its positions to line up, and one that closes up its gaps tells the reader "there is no row H" when the truth is "row H was measured and is empty". records.source: Rows and columns are the **cartesian product** of their keys' levels, empty combinations included, exactly as :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` draws empty panels: a table read by position needs its positions to line up, and one that closes up its gaps tells the reader "there is no row H" when the truth is "row H was measured and is empty". Above :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` the product is abandoned for the observed combinations only, and :attr:`PivotResult.notice` says so — an unreadable table is not more honest than a smaller one that admits what it left out.
records.translation: Las filas y las columnas son el **producto cartesiano** de los niveles de sus claves, incluidas las combinaciones vacías, exactamente igual que :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` dibuja los paneles vacíos: una tabla que se lee por posición necesita que sus posiciones estén alineadas, y una que elimina sus huecos le dice al lector "there is no row H" (no hay fila H) cuando la verdad es "row H was measured and is empty" (la fila H se midió y está vacía). records.translation: Cada celda de un :class:`PivotResult` lleva su **n**, tanto si el usuario lo marcó como si no, y el panel lo muestra. records.context: Three of those rows were bugs rather than differences of taste. Measure returned after extracting image regions again without a word when no array was loaded, so the button did nothing and said nothing. Timelapse and Motility wired ``QThread.finished`` to ``worker.deleteLater`` and dropped their own reference in the result slot — the pattern :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents as a race, and the one the Mask panel had already been fixed away from — which leaves a running ``QThread`` owned by nobody when the user closes the application view mid-pass. And Measure never told anyone its pass had landed, so no application view could react to an extracted image region preview the way it reacts to the other three.

records.source: Three of those rows were bugs rather than differences of taste. Measure returned from its re-crop without a word when no array was loaded, so the button did nothing and said nothing. Timelapse and Motility wired ``QThread.finished`` to ``worker.deleteLater`` and dropped their own reference in the result slot — the pattern :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documents as a race, and the one the Mask panel had already been fixed away from — which leaves a running ``QThread`` owned by nobody when the user closes the screen mid-pass. And Measure never told anyone its pass had landed, so no screen could react to a crop preview the way it reacts to the other three.
records.translation: Tres de esas filas eran errores y no diferencias de gusto. Measure salía de su nuevo recorte sin decir nada cuando no había ningún array cargado, de modo que el botón no hacía nada y no decía nada. Timelapse y Motility conectaban ``QThread.finished`` a ``worker.deleteLater`` y soltaban su propia referencia en la ranura del resultado (el patrón que :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.make_thread` documenta como una condición de carrera, y del que ya se había corregido el panel de Mask), lo que deja un ``QThread`` en ejecución sin propietario cuando el usuario cierra la pantalla a mitad de una pasada. Y Measure nunca avisaba de que su pasada había terminado, de modo que ninguna pantalla podía reaccionar a una vista previa de recortes como reacciona a las otras tres.

records.context: Nothing on this tab touches a processing-session folder from the main GUI execution path. On one workstation a single ``os.path.exists`` on a path under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- did not return within twenty seconds. records.source: Nothing on this tab touches a run folder from the GUI thread. On one workstation a single ``os.path.exists`` on a path under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount whose share was asleep -- did not return within twenty seconds. Every row here carries a folder the user chose, so walking, stat-ing, reading and deleting those folders (the sweep table read on a tab change, ``describe_folder``'s ``os.walk`` inside the delete confirmation, ``shutil.rmtree`` after it, and ``workspace.has_workspace`` while the row menu is built) run on a :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. The one remaining existence check -- which folder to open the chooser in -- is answered from :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`'s cache.
records.translation: Nada en esta pestaña accede a una carpeta de ejecución desde el hilo de la GUI. En una estación de trabajo, un solo ``os.path.exists`` sobre una ruta bajo ``/nas_mnt`` (un montaje ``autofs`` cuyo recurso compartido estaba en reposo) no respondió en veinte segundos. Cada fila contiene una carpeta que eligió el usuario, por lo que recorrer, consultar con stat, leer y eliminar esas carpetas (la lectura de la tabla de barrido al cambiar de pestaña, el recorrido de ``describe_folder`` con ``os.walk`` dentro de la confirmación de eliminación, el ``shutil.rmtree`` posterior y ``workspace.has_workspace`` mientras se construye el menú de la fila) se ejecuta en un :class:`spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. La única comprobación de existencia que queda (en qué carpeta abrir el selector) se responde desde la caché de :mod:`spacr.qt.path_probe`.

records.source: Unlike the general spaCR figure queue, these widgets hold the coordinate arrays themselves.  A 3-D map can therefore be spun and recoloured after it has been computed, and clicking a gallery tile opens the exact embedding that was scored rather than a PNG or a stochastic refit.
